steps.title: Prepare the rebuilt fighter
steps.text: Print at 100%, check the 50 mm ruler, and use 100–120 gsm paper. Score lightly before cutting. Grey diagonals are gentle facet folds; blue dashed lines are tab folds. These very small prototype shells need a trial build. One fighter uses 20 pieces. The cockpit and engine pods are tapered shells, not boxes.

steps.title: Form the tapered fuselage
steps.text: Form each numbered skin around an eight-sided cross-section. Close its long underside seam with the lilac tab. Then join in numerical order: tuck the next section’s small front tabs inside the previous section, matching all eight panel edges. Keep the underside seams aligned. Do not flatten the body. M01 is the dark nose. M06 is the narrow tail fairing. The front remains a tiny point-sized opening; close it with a dot of glue.

steps.title: Add the swept wings
steps.text: Fold each root tab gently underneath its wing. Glue M07 and M08 symmetrically to the fuselage sides, level with its centre line. The long root extends from 12 to 33 mm behind the nose. Leave the wings spread; their leading-edge extensions run forward beside the cockpit.

steps.title: Build both engine pods
steps.text: Form each numbered skin around an eight-sided cross-section. Close its long underside seam with the lilac tab. Then join in numerical order: tuck the next section’s small front tabs inside the previous section, matching all eight panel edges. Keep the underside seams aligned. Do not flatten the body. Make L01–L03 and R01–R03 separately. Keep their inlet and exhaust openings open. Glue the pods beneath the wing roots, centred 3.05 mm either side of the centreline, with their exhausts flush with the tail at 43.25 mm.

steps.title: Add separate tail surfaces
steps.text: Attach M09/M10 below the fins, with their roots from 33 to 40 mm behind the nose. Fold the fin feet outward and glue M11/M12 along the tops of the engine pods. The swept leading edges face forward; cant the fins slightly outward. Use small glue fillets where flat feet meet curved pods.

steps.title: Shape the rounded canopy
steps.text: Form each numbered skin around an eight-sided cross-section. Close its long underside seam with the lilac tab. Then join in numerical order: tuck the next section’s small front tabs inside the previous section, matching all eight panel edges. Keep the underside seams aligned. Do not flatten the body. The canopy is an open-bottom half-shell. Join C01 to C02, glazing facing outward. The small front end points forward. Place this canopy over the upper fuselage between 7.2 and 15 mm behind the nose. Fold its lower edge tabs inward and glue them along the upper fuselage; do not squash its rounded upper profile.

steps.title: Compare the completed silhouette
steps.text: Check the pointed nose, broad swept wings, two separate stabilizers, outward-canted fins and paired open exhausts. This is a reference-informed faceted prototype, not a dimension-certified replica. Landing gear is omitted. Trial-build before repeating the other five fighters.

steps.title: Prepare the rebuilt Hind
steps.text: Print at 100%, check the 50 mm ruler, and use 100–120 gsm paper. Score lightly before cutting. Grey diagonals are gentle facet folds; blue dashed lines are tab folds. These very small prototype shells need a trial build. One helicopter uses 20 pieces. The cockpit steps and narrow tail boom are built into the shell sections.

steps.title: Build the stepped cockpit
steps.text: Form each numbered skin around an eight-sided cross-section. Close its long underside seam with the lilac tab. Then join in numerical order: tuck the next section’s small front tabs inside the previous section, matching all eight panel edges. Keep the underside seams aligned. Do not flatten the body. H01–H04 make the chin and two cockpit bulges. Keep the blue glazing on top; the underside seams align below the chin.

steps.title: Form the cabin and tail boom
steps.text: Form each numbered skin around an eight-sided cross-section. Close its long underside seam with the lilac tab. Then join in numerical order: tuck the next section’s small front tabs inside the previous section, matching all eight panel edges. Keep the underside seams aligned. Do not flatten the body. Continue with H05–H09. H06 is the wide cabin; H08 narrows sharply into the tail boom. Keep the boom rising toward the tail, as shown in Side view.

steps.title: Build the engine fairings
steps.text: Form each numbered skin around an eight-sided cross-section. Close its long underside seam with the lilac tab. Then join in numerical order: tuck the next section’s small front tabs inside the previous section, matching all eight panel edges. Keep the underside seams aligned. Do not flatten the body. H17–H18 form the left engine and H19–H20 the right. Glue the paired rounded pods along the cabin roof from 7.5 to 20 mm behind the nose. Centre them 1.2 mm either side of the centreline; the smaller intake ends face forward.

steps.title: Fit the drooping stub wings
steps.text: Fold H10/H11 root tabs upward. Glue them to the cabin sides from 15 to 20.5 mm behind the nose. Their tips slope slightly downward, about 1 mm below the wing roots. Do not make them horizontal like the old edition.

steps.title: Build the tail assembly
steps.text: Glue the centre of H12 across the tail boom at 35 mm behind the nose. Attach the H13 foot to the boom tip so the fin sweeps upward and aft. Glue H16 to the left side of the fin near its upper end. The three-blade rotor stays fixed.

steps.title: Add the main rotor
steps.text: Form H14 into an octagonal sleeve and glue its seam. Stand it upright between the engine fairings, 15 mm behind the nose. Glue its lower edges to the inner upper surfaces of the fairings; use a small glue fillet to bridge the curved contact. Glue only H15’s central hub to its top. Keep all five blades level. Its swept diameter is 43.25 mm; do not enlarge the rotor separately.

steps.title: Check the Hind profile
steps.text: Compare Side and Top views: two stepped cockpit bulges, a deep cabin, downward-sloping stub wings and a much thinner rising tail boom. The Mi-24 remains a custom display addition to the carrier. This paper prototype still needs a physical fit test; landing gear and small equipment are omitted.
